games.headline: Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup beats The Canberra Mob
article: Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup beat The Canberra Mob 118.10 to 97.40 in Week 2, a solid win decided by 20.70 points.

Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup put up 118.10 this week, 5.2 over their projected 112.8 and the 3rd-highest score of the week. Dak Prescott carried them with 37.6 points, about a quarter of the team's total, 13.0 over his projection. Jonathan Taylor (27.2) and Travis Kelce (20.6) were the other big contributors.
The Canberra Mob managed 97.40 this week, 8.9 under their projected 106.3. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 31.3, and 49ers D/ST added 12.0.
The letdown for The Canberra Mob was Justin Herbert, who managed 9.2 on a 23.0 projection.
Not much The Canberra Mob could have done about this one: even their best possible lineup (98.00) wouldn't have caught Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup.
Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup could have scored even more by starting Jake Ferguson (18.3) instead of David Montgomery (3.4) and Chuba Hubbard (13.4) instead of Jeremiyah Love (6.0).
At quarterback, Dak Prescott (37.6) outdueled Justin Herbert (9.2).
Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup improves to 1-1 (5th place). The Canberra Mob drops to 1-1 (8th).
Next week, Cleo's Purrrfect Lineup faces Ken (0-2), who are coming off a 37.6-point loss to Stroud and Proud.
Next week, The Canberra Mob faces I Call Gibbs (2-0), who are coming off an 85.7-point win over K9 Unit.

games.headline: King Henry cruises past * Go Buckeyes
article: King Henry beat * Go Buckeyes 100.80 to 79.20 in Week 2, a solid win decided by 21.60 points.
Lamar Jackson carried them with 16.4 points, 8.5 under his projection. Derrick Henry (16.2) and Terrance Ferguson (14.4) were the other big contributors.
* Go Buckeyes managed 79.20 this week, 16.7 under their projected 95.9 and the 3rd-lowest score of the week. Daniel Jones led the way with 13.0, and Spencer Shrader added 12.0.
The letdown for * Go Buckeyes was Alec Pierce, who managed 1.6 on a 9.2 projection.

Here's the painful part for * Go Buckeyes: starting Bryce Young (29.6) instead of Daniel Jones (13.0) and Chris Godwin Jr. (7.3) instead of Alec Pierce (1.6) would have produced 105.10 points, enough to win.
King Henry could have scored even more by starting Dalton Kincaid (19.0) instead of Kyle Pitts Sr. (2.0) and Josh Downs (10.7) instead of George Pickens (7.0).
At quarterback, Lamar Jackson (16.4) outdueled Daniel Jones (13.0).

Going into Monday night, King Henry led by 0.70, and * Go Buckeyes still had Cam Skattebo to play. Cam Skattebo (7.5) put in work, but King Henry's Terrance Ferguson (14.4) and Rams D/ST (14.0) more than answered.
King Henry improves to 1-1 (6th place). * Go Buckeyes drops to 0-2 (12th).
Next week, King Henry faces Oops (1-1), who are coming off a 40.8-point loss to The Dude Abides.
Next week, * Go Buckeyes faces Dena's Team 🏈 (1-1), who are coming off a 42.8-point loss to Slim Shiesties.

The letdown for Oops was Jaxson Dart, who managed 0.0 on a 21.0 projection. Oops might have a quarterback decision to make if Dart doesn't figure it out: Patrick Mahomes is sitting right there on the bench (and scored 34.7 this week).
